Candle.what: A candle shows a whole {period} of trading in one shape, drawn from four prices.
Candle.body: The open is the price at the start of the {period} and the close is the price at its end. The body of the candle spans the two.
Candle.wicks: The high and the low are the furthest the price went during the {period}. The thin lines above and below the body are wicks, and they reach to them.
Candle.colour: A candle that closes above its open is green. A candle that closes below its open is red. One that closes where it opened has no body, and is neither.
SuccessiveCandles.what: Candles of one colour that follow one another are Successive Candles, counted from the first of the colour to the last.
SuccessiveCandles.count: How many in a row are worth marking is a setting on the page, not part of the term.
Point.HH: A Higher High (HH) is a high of the Sawtooth at one order that is higher than the high before it at that order.
Point.HL: A Higher Low (HL) is a low of the Sawtooth at one order that is higher than the low before it at that order.
Point.LH: A Lower High (LH) is a high of the Sawtooth at one order that is lower than the high before it at that order.
Point.LL: A Lower Low (LL) is a low of the Sawtooth at one order that is lower than the low before it at that order.
Point.closes: Highs and lows are read from the closes.
Point.moving: The latest high or low is not fixed: while the price keeps closing beyond it, it moves on to each new close.
Sawtooth.what: Joining the highs and lows at one order gives a Sawtooth: a less noisy, lower-resolution version of the closes.
Sawtooth.legs: Each line of the Sawtooth is a leg: an Upleg when it rises, a Downleg when it falls.
Sawtooth.orders: Each order has a Sawtooth of its own, finer than the order before it.
Swing.what: A Swing is a range of positions. It begins at the position that the BoS breaks, and ends at the BoS itself.
Swing.candidate: Until the BoS happens it is only a Candidate Swing. The BoS Confirms it.
Swing.direction: {a swing} is a Swing that trends {trends}.
Swing.turn: The {turn} is the {extreme} position in the Swing. It is either {turn labels}.
Swing.legs: {a swing} is characterised by {a first leg} from the {start} to the {turn}, followed by {a second leg} from the {turn} to the BoS.
Swing.bos: A BoS closes beyond the position its Swing begins at.
Swing.msb: An MSB closes beyond the Swing Low or Swing High of a Swing that is already Confirmed.
Swing.against: A BoS continues in the direction of its Swing; an MSB goes against it.
Swing.confirms: A BoS Confirms a Swing; an MSB Confirms nothing. It remains an observation.
Swing.count: Every Swing has exactly one BoS; a Swing has at most one MSB, and may have none.
Swing.strong: {a swing} with an MSB inside it is a Weak {swing}. {a swing} with none is a Strong {swing}.
Swing.weak: A Weak {swing} always has an {weak turn} as its {turn}, because the MSB took the price {beyond} the {turn} before it.
BoS.close: A wick beyond a level is not a BoS. A BoS needs a close beyond it.
MSB.before: An MSB refers to the prior {turn}, and so can be observed before a new Swing is Confirmed.
MSB.close: A wick beyond a level is not an MSB. An MSB needs a close beyond it.
MSB.alias: A Market Structure Break is sometimes called a Change of Character.
Ghost.what: Something we observed in real time that later disappears with new data is called a Ghost.
Trend.what: A Trend is two or more Swings in a row in one direction: {a trend} is a run of {swing}s, and begins where its first {swing} begins.
Trend.confirmed: The BoS of the second {swing} makes two in a row: that Confirms the {trend}.
Trend.next: After an MSB against a Trend, the next BoS decides. {a swing}'s BoS continues the {trend} with a Weak {swing}. {a other swing}'s BoS ends it.
Trend.strength: The Strength of a Trend is the share of its Swings that are Strong.
Trend.ends: A Trend ends at the BoS of the first Swing in the opposite direction.
Trend.count: Like Successive Candles, a Trend is a count of what has happened. It does not say what the price will do next.
Retracement.what: A Retracement measures how far a Swing's counter-move has come back along the move before it: 0% where the Swing begins, 100% at the Swing Low or Swing High of the Swing before it in the same direction.
Retracement.reading: It is a reading, and Confirms nothing. A close at 100% or more is an MSB; a close beyond where the Swing began is its BoS.
Retracement.marked: Which readings are marked is a setting on the page, not part of the term.
Retracement.small: A move smaller than 0.1% of its price gives no reading.
Range.what: A Range is a deep Retracement whose own structure has broken: one order finer, an MSB closes against it before the Swing's BoS. How deep is a setting on the page.
Range.box: Its box runs from where the Swing began to the furthest close of the Retracement at that moment, with a band either side, a share of the box's height set on the page.
Range.holds: The Range holds while the price closes inside the bands.
Range.ends: It ends at the first close beyond a band. A BoS or MSB inside the bands does not end it.
Strategy.what: A strategy is a set of rules for trading, written down exactly so that it can be tested: when to enter a trade, and where its Take Profit and Stop Loss are set.
Trade.what: A trade is entered at one price and closed later at another, for a gain or a loss.
Trade.entry: A strategy enters a trade when its entry condition is met. The condition is read at the close of each candle, from that candle and the ones before it alone, and the trade is entered at that close.
Trade.chain: An entry condition can be a chain of steps. Each step is looked for only once the one before it is met, and only within as many candles of it as the strategy allows. The trade is entered when the last step is met, and the next trade needs the whole chain again.
Risk.what: A trade's reward is how far its Take Profit is from its entry: what it wins if the Take Profit is reached. Its risk is how far its Stop Loss is from its entry: what it loses if the Stop Loss is reached.
Risk.ratio: R is the unit of risk: 1R is how far the Stop Loss is from the entry. The reward is counted in R, so a Take Profit twice as far from the entry as the Stop Loss is a 2R target.
Risk.breakeven: A trade that wins its target in R or loses 1R breaks even over many trades when the share it wins is one divided by one plus its target: half at 1R, a third at 2R.
Trade.takeProfit: A trade's Take Profit is set as it is entered: the price where it closes with a gain, above the entry for a long trade and below it for a short one.
Trade.stopLoss: A trade's Stop Loss is set as it is entered: the price where it closes with a loss, below the entry for a long trade and above it for a short one.
Trade.outcome: Whichever exit the price reaches first ends the trade. From the next candle on, each candle is checked against the exits.
Trade.exits: When it reaches the Take Profit, the trade closes there with a gain; when it reaches the Stop Loss, it closes there with a loss.
Trade.gap: A candle that opens beyond an exit closes the trade at its open.
Trade.both: A candle that reaches both exits cannot say which came first, so it counts as the Stop Loss.
